paragraphs.text: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffeth up, but love edifieth.
paragraphs.original: Περὶ δὲ τῶν εἰδωλοθύτων, οἴδαμεν ὅτι πάντες γνῶσιν ἔχομεν. ἡ γνῶσις φυσιοῖ, ἡ δὲ ἀγάπη οἰκοδομεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: Peri de tōn eidōlothytōn, oidamen hoti pantes gnōsin echomen. hē gnōsis physioi, hē de agapē oikodomei.

paragraphs.text: If any man thinketh that he knoweth anything, he knoweth not yet as he ought to know;
paragraphs.original: εἴ τις δοκεῖ ἐγνωκέναι τι, οὔπω ἔγνω καθὼς δεῖ γνῶναι·
paragraphs.translit: ei tis dokei egnōkenai ti, oupō egnō kathōs dei gnōnai·

paragraphs.text: but if any man loveth God, the same is known by him.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δέ τις ἀγαπᾷ τὸν θεόν, οὗτος ἔγνωσται ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ei de tis agapa ton theon, houtos egnōstai hypʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: Concerning therefore the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that no idol is [anything] in the world, and that there is no God but one.
paragraphs.original: Περὶ τῆς βρώσεως οὖν τῶν εἰδωλοθύτων οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὐδὲν εἴδωλον ἐν κόσμῳ, καὶ ὅτι οὐδεὶς θεὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς.
paragraphs.translit: Peri tēs brōseōs oun tōn eidōlothytōn oidamen hoti ouden eidōlon en kosmō, kai hoti oudeis theos ei mē heis.

paragraphs.text: For though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or on earth; as there are gods many, and lords many;
paragraphs.original: καὶ γὰρ εἴπερ εἰσὶν λεγόμενοι θεοὶ εἴτε ἐν οὐρανῷ εἴτε ἐπὶ γῆς, ὥσπερ εἰσὶν θεοὶ πολλοὶ καὶ κύριοι πολλοί,
paragraphs.translit: kai gar eiper eisin legomenoi theoi eite en ouranō eite epi gēs, hōsper eisin theoi polloi kai kyrioi polloi,

paragraphs.text: yet to us there is one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we unto him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through him.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ ἡμῖν εἷς θεὸς ὁ πατήρ, ἐξ οὗ τὰ πάντα καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς αὐτόν, καὶ εἷς κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, διʼ οὗ τὰ πάντα καὶ ἡμεῖς διʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: allʼ hēmin heis theos ho patēr, ex hou ta panta kai hēmeis eis auton, kai heis kyrios Iēsous Christos, diʼ hou ta panta kai hēmeis diʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: Howbeit there is not in all men that knowledge: but some, being used until now to the idol, eat as [of] a thing sacrificed to an idol; and their conscience being weak is defiled.
paragraphs.original: Ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἐν πᾶσιν ἡ γνῶσις· τινὲς δὲ τῇ συνηθείᾳ ἕως ἄρτι τοῦ εἰδώλου ὡς εἰδωλόθυτον ἐσθίουσιν, καὶ ἡ συνείδησις αὐτῶν ἀσθενὴς οὖσα μολύνεται.
paragraphs.translit: Allʼ ouk en pasin hē gnōsis· tines de tē synētheia heōs arti tou eidōlou hōs eidōlothyton esthiousin, kai hē syneidēsis autōn asthenēs ousa molynetai.

paragraphs.text: But food will not commend us to God: neither, if we eat not, are we the worse; nor, if we eat, are we the better.
paragraphs.original: βρῶμα δὲ ἡμᾶς οὐ παραστήσει τῷ θεῷ· οὔτε γὰρ ἐὰν φάγωμεν, περισσεύομεν, οὔτε ἐὰν μὴ φάγωμεν, ὑστερούμεθα.
paragraphs.translit: brōma de hēmas ou parastēsei tō theō· oute gar ean phagōmen, perisseuomen, oute ean mē phagōmen, hysteroumetha.

paragraphs.text: But take heed lest by any means this liberty of yours become a stumblingblock to the weak.
paragraphs.original: βλέπετε δὲ μή πως ἡ ἐξουσία ὑμῶν αὕτη πρόσκομμα γένηται τοῖς ἀσθενέσιν.
paragraphs.translit: blepete de mē pōs hē exousia hymōn hautē proskomma genētai tois asthenesin.

paragraphs.text: For if a man see thee who hast knowledge sitting at meat in an idol`s temple, will not his conscience, if he is weak, be emboldened to eat things sacrificed to idols?
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν γάρ τις ἴδῃ σὲ τὸν ἔχοντα γνῶσιν ἐν εἰδωλείῳ κατακείμενον, οὐχὶ ἡ συνείδησις αὐτοῦ ἀσθενοῦς ὄντος οἰκοδομηθήσεται εἰς τὸ τὰ εἰδωλόθυτα ἐσθίειν;
paragraphs.translit: ean gar tis idē se ton echonta gnōsin en eidōleiō katakeimenon, ouchi hē syneidēsis autou asthenous ontos oikodomēthēsetai eis to ta eidōlothyta esthiein;

paragraphs.text: For through thy knowledge he that is weak perisheth, the brother for whose sake Christ died.
paragraphs.original: ἀπόλλυται γὰρ ὁ ἀσθενῶν ἐν τῇ σῇ γνώσει, ὁ ἀδελφὸς διʼ ὃν Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν.
paragraphs.translit: apollytai gar ho asthenōn en tē sē gnōsei, ho adelphos diʼ hon Christos apethanen.

paragraphs.text: And thus, sinning against the brethren, and wounding their conscience when it is weak, ye sin against Christ.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως δὲ ἁμαρτάνοντες εἰς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ τύπτοντες αὐτῶν τὴν συνείδησιν ἀσθενοῦσαν εἰς Χριστὸν ἁμαρτάνετε.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs de hamartanontes eis tous adelphous kai typtontes autōn tēn syneidēsin asthenousan eis Christon hamartanete.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore, if meat causeth my brother to stumble, I will eat no flesh for evermore, that I cause not my brother to stumble.
paragraphs.original: διόπερ εἰ βρῶμα σκανδαλίζει τὸν ἀδελφόν μου, οὐ μὴ φάγω κρέα εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἵνα μὴ τὸν ἀδελφόν μου σκανδαλίσω.
paragraphs.translit: dioper ei brōma skandalizei ton adelphon mou, ou mē phagō krea eis ton aiōna, hina mē ton adelphon mou skandalisō.
